question: The US Air Force measured 4,063 pilots on ten body dimensions. How many fell in the middle 30% of every one?
answer: None. Gilbert Daniels found that not one of the 4,063 pilots was in the middle 30% on all ten measures, and fewer than 4 in 100 matched on just three. Everyone was ordinary in some ways and unusual in others, so a cockpit built for the average pilot fitted nobody.
move: Ask how many people match the typical profile on everything at once.
trap: Expecting the typical pilot to be typical in everything at once.
reference: Daniels, The 'Average Man'?, Technical Note WCRD 53-7, Wright Air Development Center, 1952
